boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the Lackawanna Avenue/Cliff Street downtown corridor, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Steamtown National Historic Site
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter at Lackawanna Avenue and Cliff Street, then use the site’s visitor information to choose a self-guided rail-history stop.
cards.short_summary: A downtown railroad site preserving and interpreting steam railroading.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the public entrance at Lackawanna Avenue and Cliff Street and describes Steamtown as preserving steam-railroading history.
cards.access_notes: Current public hours listed by NPS: Wednesday–Sunday, 9:30 a.m.–4 p.m.; check the official page before visiting.

cards.title: 1902/1937 Roundhouse
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the designated public areas at Steamtown to view the roundhouse and keep clear of operational railroad equipment.
cards.short_summary: A named historic roundhouse within Steamtown’s public complex.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS lists the 1902/1937 Roundhouse among the areas currently open to the public at Steamtown.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted safety guidance because Steamtown is a working railroad site.

cards.title: History Museum at Steamtown
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Start indoors with the history displays, then continue into the railyard only through designated visitor areas.
cards.short_summary: An indoor museum stop focused on railroad history.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS lists the History Museum as an area open to the public at Steamtown.
cards.access_notes: Check current park operations before traveling; access can change with railroad operations.

cards.title: Turntable Area
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk to the designated turntable viewing area and photograph from public paths without stepping on rails or equipment.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor Steamtown area centered on railroad turning infrastructure.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS lists the Turntable Area among Steamtown’s public areas and its brochure identifies a 90-foot turntable used for turning engines.
cards.access_notes: Use designated areas only; NPS advises visitors to watch for moving trains and vehicles.

cards.title: Steamtown Railyard
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow the marked public route through the railyard and plan for gravel, tracks, and uneven ground underfoot.
cards.short_summary: The historic yard is the outdoor setting for locomotives and railroad infrastructure.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS describes Steamtown as a former Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Scranton yard and lists designated railyard areas as public.
cards.access_notes: This is an active railroad environment; remain in designated public areas and watch for moving vehicles.

cards.title: Steamtown Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Make the Visitor Center your first stop for orientation, current operations, and an indoor place to begin the visit.
cards.short_summary: A documented starting point for present-day Steamtown visits.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS states that the Visitor Center is a public starting point for information and services on days the outdoor kiosk is not open.
cards.source_title: Steamtown Visitor Center Reopens for Summer Season
cards.access_notes: NPS says park hours are 9:30 a.m.–5 p.m. daily in its seasonal notice; verify current operations before arrival.

cards.title: Technology Museum at Steamtown
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Look for the tactile steam-engine cutaway and other accessibility-focused interpretive displays inside the Technology Museum.
cards.short_summary: An indoor interpretive stop with tactile exhibit access.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies a tactile steam-engine cutaway and other tactile exhibits in Steamtown’s Technology Museum.
cards.access_notes: Contact Steamtown for current accessibility details or assistance.

cards.title: Big Boy No. 4012
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the current Steamtown page for this locomotive’s display status, then view it only from authorized visitor space.
cards.short_summary: A named surviving Big Boy locomotive documented at Steamtown.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies Big Boy No. 4012 as one of eight surviving Big Boys and the only one in the eastern United States.
cards.access_notes: Display and access conditions may change; follow current NPS instructions on site.

cards.title: Baldwin Locomotive Works No. 26
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the current train-ride page to see whether No. 26 is operating, and treat the locomotive as a viewing subject when rides are unavailable.
cards.short_summary: A specifically named historic locomotive associated with Steamtown operations.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS’s current train-ride page identifies Steamtown’s Baldwin Locomotive Works No. 26.
cards.source_title: Train Rides - Steamtown National Historic Site
cards.access_notes: Train operations, weather, equipment, and crew availability can change; check the official schedule.

cards.title: Tickets and Information Kiosk
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue at Cliff Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the kiosk to confirm day-of operations and, when available, purchase short-ride tickets with card payment.
cards.short_summary: A named on-site information point for current train operations.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS states that short train-ride tickets are available at Steamtown’s Tickets and Information Kiosk when rides operate.
cards.source_title: Train Rides - Steamtown National Historic Site
cards.access_notes: The kiosk is tied to train operations; confirm availability on the official page before going.

warnings: All cards use the Lackawanna Avenue/Cliff Street downtown corridor and are distinct named destinations within Steamtown National Historic Site.
